beats.story: On Saturday, my carefully curated day of nothing is interrupted by heavy pounding on my door. "Mom, what the hell?" I say as I open it, taking in her frustrated expression. She's all dolled up with thick eyeliner and glowing pink lipstick. She puts a hand on her hip. "It's almost time for dinner. You're in your pajamas?" "It's loungewear," I say uselessly. "Why are you here?" "We're going to dinner with the Habibs," she says, like I should have known this the whole time. "What?" I sputter.
beats.story_cn: 周六，我精心策划的“无所事事日”被一阵擂门声打断。“妈，搞什么名堂？”我边开门边抱怨，迎面撞见她一脸焦躁。她浓妆艳抹，粗黑眼线配着亮粉唇膏，单手叉腰：“晚饭时间快到了，你还穿睡衣？”“这是家居服。”我无力地辩解，“您怎么来了？”“跟哈比卜家约了晚餐。”她说得理所当然，仿佛我早该知道这回事。“什么？”我差点咬到舌头。

beats.story: "No, we're not." I've been peppering her with little comments about Armin being annoying all week. How does that translate into unplanned group dinners? "Yes, Armin's mom and I arranged it. Get dressed, don't keep them waiting. We're not a rude family." She herds me toward my bedroom with shooing hands with the efficiency of a border collie. As soon as I'm inside, I grab my phone and text Armin: We're having dinner?! The reply comes almost instantly: They didn't tell me either until a second ago! When my mom ushers me into the car, my dad is sitting in the driver's seat.
beats.story_cn: “才不是。”我这一周没少跟她抱怨阿明有多烦人。这怎么就变成了临时家庭聚餐？“是阿明妈妈和我安排的。快换衣服，别让人家等，我们家可不兴失礼。”她像赶牧羊犬般把我推向卧室。刚进门我就抓起手机给阿明发消息：咱们要一起吃饭？！回复秒到：他们也是刚告诉我！母亲把我塞进车里时，父亲早已坐在驾驶座上。

beats.story: He at least has the decency to look apologetic. At the restaurant, the table holding our party shines like a beacon from the foyer. The Habibs are already sitting down, Armin looking miserable beside his parents. My mom nudges me into the chair opposite Armin and then takes the seat beside him. He's sandwiched between moms. I pull my phone out underneath the tablecloth. Shit. They have us separated.
beats.story_cn: 至少他还知道摆出歉疚神情。餐厅里，我们那桌在门厅处亮如灯塔。哈比卜一家已落座，阿明愁眉苦脸地挨着父母。母亲把我推到阿明对面的椅子，自己坐到他身侧。他被夹在两位母亲中间。我掀起桌布下摸出手机——糟了，他们故意把我们隔开了。

beats.story: Armin's jaw clenches. His reply comes a moment later. It's okay, just don't say anything too specific. Then a second text: We can do this. Just keep chill. My mom calls, "Isn't it nice to be a big family together with the bride and groom!" And she and Armin's dad stand up and clap, loud and hollow through the room. It's like dominoes: the servers and some patrons build on to their claps, drumming a surprisingly loud vibration. Even the guy eating alone at a table in the corner smacks his thighs.
beats.story_cn: 阿尔敏下颌紧绷。片刻后他回复道：没事，别说得太具体。紧接着又发来一条：我们能应付。保持冷静。我妈嚷道：“新郎新娘和大家团聚多美好啊！”她和阿尔敏的父亲起身鼓掌，空洞的拍手声在房间里回荡。如同多米诺骨牌般，侍应生和几位食客也跟着拍起手来，汇成惊人的轰响。就连角落独自用餐的食客也拍了下大腿。

beats.story: So far so chill. My mom tugs at Armin's sleeve and goes in to kiss both his cheeks while his mom grins widely. A drink is placed in his hand, and a giant pot of lamb stew is spooned onto his waiting plate, appearing as if by magic -- only really it's by fawning middle-aged mothers. "So, baby, how is work going?" Armin's mom asks him. Armin's eyes flash my way as he takes a long sip of his water. "Very good. We're going to have one of the best Q2s I've ever seen and are forecasting a lot of returns on investments." I almost spit out my own water. Damn, that was believable.
beats.story_cn: 目前还算顺利。我妈拽着阿尔敏的袖子凑上前亲他双颊，他母亲笑得合不拢嘴。有人给他递了杯酒，一大锅羊肉炖像变戏法似的舀进他面前的盘子——当然那不是魔法，是中年母亲们奉承的杰作。“孩子，工作还顺利吗？”阿尔敏的母亲问道。阿尔敏的目光向我飞来，同时啜了一大口水。“非常顺利。我们将迎来我职业生涯中第二季度最佳业绩，预计投资回报率会非常可观。”我差点把水喷出来。见鬼，简直演得太像了。

beats.story: The moms look at him with absolute glee. "Here," his mom says, tearing a piece of bread and adding it to his plate, then pushing over the bowl of eggplant dip I was just eyeing for myself. "You need to eat." Holy shit, of course! How did I not realize before? Armin is a doodool tala. Direct translation: "golden penis" (because of course). Basically, he's a mama's boy who can do no wrong and must not lift a finger in the process. Even worse, he's a doodool tala who hasn't become a doctor or lawyer -- or accounting executive -- even as his mom is ailing.
beats.story_cn: 两位母亲眉开眼笑地看着他。“给，”他母亲撕下一块面包放进他餐盘，又把我刚才惦记的茄子酱推过去，“你得好好吃饭。”天啊！我怎么早没想到？阿尔敏是个金贵独苗（直译：金色命根，果然名副其实）。基本上就是那种永远正确的妈宝男，十指不沾阳春水。更糟的是，这金贵独苗没成为医生、律师——或会计高管——连母亲病中也依然如故。

beats.story: It's a wonder his bullshit isn't wilder. I smile toward Armin. "All the bosses ask Armin to lead their projects. He's the most precise and efficient." Two impressive buzzwords. "Ahhh," all the parents hum. Armin shoots me a grateful smile. "Well, Jolene has the best ideas. I was talking to Gregory -- my second-in-command -- and apparently head office was so impressed by her suggestion at a recent meeting that they may implement it across Canada." My face flushes because Armin doesn't sound like he's lying this time.
beats.story_cn: 他的胡说八道居然没更离谱，真是个奇迹。我朝阿尔明微笑。“所有老板都请阿尔明负责他们的项目。他最精准高效。”两个令人印象深刻的流行词。“啊哈，”所有家长哼声赞同。阿尔明投来感激的微笑。“嗯，乔琳有最好的点子。我和格雷戈里——我的副手——聊天，显然总部对她最近会议上提出的建议印象深刻，可能在整个加拿大推行。”我的脸红了，因为阿尔明这次听起来不像是在撒谎。

beats.story: "Jolene's always been a very innovative thinker." This comment comes from my dad, and it's his proud grin that hits me the hardest. He continues: "When she was a kid, she helped design the shelves for her mom's spice rack." Mom claps. "And I made so many good meals because of this." She pats Armin's hand that's sitting on the table. "Don't worry, I'll teach Jolene to cook better. Is that the problem?" Armin opens his mouth in surprise, but before he can respond his mom cuts in: "Jolene is so beautiful. Did you notice her right away?" Armin grins. "Absolutely. I couldn't help it.
beats.story_cn: “乔琳一直是个很有创新思维的思考者。”这句评论来自我父亲，他骄傲的笑容最让我心痛。他继续说：“她小时候，帮她妈妈设计了香料架的架子。”妈妈鼓掌。“而且我因此做了那么多好吃的。”她拍拍阿尔明放在桌上的手。“别担心，我会教乔琳更好地做饭。是这个问题吗？”阿尔明惊讶地张开嘴，但他还没来得及回应，他妈妈插嘴：“乔琳很漂亮。你一眼就注意到了吗？”阿尔明咧嘴一笑。“当然。我忍不住。”

beats.story: Tried asking her to go for poutine, but she shut me down." "Good girl," they all chant. My gaze draws to Armin again. The poutine story really happened too. Was he actually doing that when we first met? My skin flushes, and the room is suddenly warmer. Obviously, we're not like that now, but how many things -- how much -- have I missed? It's an odd type of melancholy that washes over me as they all laugh around me. I think of the girl I was when I first started at the office, all the experiences and chances I've denied her.
beats.story_cn: “试图请她去吃肉汁奶酪薯条，但她拒绝了。”“好女孩，”他们齐声说。我的目光再次转向阿尔明。肉汁奶酪薯条的故事确实发生过。我们初次见面时他真的是那样吗？我的皮肤发红，房间突然变暖。显然，我们现在不是那样了，但有多少事——多少——我错过了？当他们在我周围大笑时，一种奇怪的忧郁笼罩着我。我想起刚来办公室时的那个女孩，所有我拒绝给她的经历和机会。

Armin seems to relax into the idea. And there is a part of me that would really love for it to all be true. I mean, obviously not the Armin part -- the ship that was my ability to find him even remotely attractive sailed away a long time ago. But it's the way our families are meshing, the comfort of being with a group of people who all like one another. My mom's high shoulders, the rare softness in my dad's expressions. I haven't thought about the mess at the office once since I sat down.
beats.story_cn: “我当然能做出和你妈妈一样美味的东西。”阿尔敏微笑道，“只要不麻烦您。”“不麻烦。我会让乔琳在公司带给你。”阿尔敏似乎放松了些许。而我内心深处，竟真的渴望这一切成真。倒不是指阿尔敏——那艘承载我对他产生丝毫好感的小船早已远航。而是这种家庭交融的氛围，与一群彼此投缘的人共处的舒适感。母亲舒展的肩线，父亲难得柔和的神情。从落座至今，我完全忘记了办公室里的那堆烂摊子。

"Our families have made very good friends in a short time, and we are both very proud you found each other." Armin and I smile, the unease cracking our grins. Her husband puts a supportive hand on her thin shoulder. "I know you don't want to plan a party now, but I'm afraid I might not be around for the wedding if it takes too long." Crap. My chest tightens as Armin's eyes flash toward me, his lips downturned.

With the bill taken care of, Armin's dad begins to help his wife out of her seat. My parents come around to help too, my dad pushing over the wheelchair and my mom making sure the Habibs have plenty of to-go containers with the extra sauces. I slide into the empty chair next to Armin. Before I can speak, he says, "I know, I know. But she's so happy." We both look toward our parents, who are now moving toward the door together, laughing at something Armin's mom said. Without really thinking, I say, "Is this really what she needs?" My heartbeat picks up when Armin's eyes lock on me.
beats.story_cn: 当账单夹着薄荷糖飘然而至，两位父亲几乎要上演全武行。阿尔明劈手夺过，坚持用他的高管薪水支付。账单了结后，阿尔明搀扶母亲离座。我父母也过来帮忙——父亲推着轮椅，母亲仔细地为哈比布一家打包剩余的酱料。我滑进阿尔明身旁的空位，未及开口，他先低语道："我懂，我懂。可她那么开心。"我们望着父母们说笑走向门口，阿尔明母亲刚讲的笑话让他们笑作一团。我不假思索地问："但这真是她需要的吗？"当阿尔明的目光骤然锁住我时，心跳陡然加速。

beats.story: Like, to her, you're Carl. To my mom, I'm Carl. You know?" "Fuck you." His laugh has a manic tinge. A wave of relief hits as the laughter pulls through me too. He gets up. "Okay. Yeah, I get your point a little. Even though I could've lived without the Carl comparison." He looks toward his mom again. "Just give me a little more time. I just want her to know I'm okay." I smile.
beats.story_cn: “比如说在她眼里你是卡尔。在我妈心里，我就是卡尔。明白吗？”“操你的。”他的笑声里带着癫狂感。当笑声也感染了我时，一股解脱的浪潮席卷而来。他起身道：“好吧，我大概懂你意思了。虽然我本可以不听这卡尔类比。”他又望向母亲那边，“再给我点时间。我只想让她知道我很好。”我露出微笑。
